categories.name: AI Agent Security & Vulnerabilities
categories.summary: A significant focus on agentic AI security emerged today, with multiple reports highlighting critical vulnerabilities in AI coding assistants and production agents. Research shows only 11% of production AI agents meet security standards, while specific CVEs and attack vectors targeting IDE tools and supply chains were disclosed. The common thread is the danger of treating untrusted content as trusted instructions.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-10591: Kiro IDE file-write vulnerability enables code execution
key_items.detail: AWS disclosed a vulnerability where the Kiro IDE's file-write tool can write to execution-sensitive paths, turning file operations into command execution when driven by untrusted instructions.

key_items.title: Only 11% of production AI agents pass security assessments
key_items.detail: Assessment of 100 production AI agents reveals widespread susceptibility to 'hostile document' takeover where untrusted content can steer tool use under standing credentials.

key_items.title: Poisoning Claude Code via GitHub Issues
key_items.detail: Flatt Security research demonstrates how a single malicious GitHub issue can compromise the AI coding assistant supply chain through prompt injection.

categories.name: Prompt Injection & Supply Chain Attacks
categories.summary: Supply chain security for AI systems took center stage with reports of protestware leveraging prompt injection techniques. The jqwik 1.10.0 incident demonstrates a novel attack vector using terminal escape codes to hide malicious instructions from human review while targeting agentic coding tools that parse logs.

key_items.title: Protestware in jqwik 1.10.0 uses prompt injection against AI agents
key_items.detail: A supply-chain attack embeds terminal escape codes that hide malicious instructions from humans but remain visible to AI agents parsing build output, highlighting the need to treat build logs as untrusted input.

categories.name: AI Governance & Frameworks
categories.summary: OWASP released version 2.01 of their State of Agentic AI Security and Governance report, providing updated control mappings that bridge agent security concerns with regulatory frameworks. This resource helps organizations translate responsible AI goals into actionable governance policies and assurance artifacts.

key_items.title: OWASP State of Agentic AI Security and Governance v2.01
key_items.detail: Updated framework document mapping agentic system security controls to governance requirements and regulatory expectations for practical policy implementation.

categories.name: Industry News & Legal Developments
categories.summary: OpenAI faces significant legal pressure as Florida filed a lawsuit against the company and CEO Sam Altman, alleging they concealed ChatGPT risks from users. This represents escalating regulatory and legal scrutiny of major AI providers.

key_items.title: Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over hidden ChatGPT risks
key_items.detail: The state of Florida filed a lawsuit claiming OpenAI deliberately hid risks associated with ChatGPT from its users, marking increased legal action against AI companies.

categories.name: Government AI Policy
categories.summary: The White House issued new presidential actions focused on promoting advanced AI innovation while addressing security concerns, signaling continued federal engagement with AI governance at the highest levels.

key_items.title: White House Presidential Action on AI Innovation and Security
key_items.detail: New executive guidance on balancing advanced AI development with security requirements, continuing the administration's AI policy agenda.

categories.name: Security Research & Analysis
categories.summary: Technical security research covered credential theft vectors and industry skill gaps. Trail of Bits published analysis on skill distribution challenges in the security field, while research on GitHub token stealing techniques highlighted ongoing risks in developer tooling.

key_items.title: GitHub Token Stealing Techniques
key_items.detail: Technical blog post detailing methods for stealing GitHub tokens, relevant for securing CI/CD pipelines and developer environments.

key_items.title: Trail of Bits on Security Skill Distribution
key_items.detail: Analysis of the current state of skill distribution in the security industry, highlighting systemic challenges in building security capabilities.

top_insights: Agentic AI security is reaching a critical inflection point—with only 11% of production agents passing security assessments, the gap between deployment velocity and security maturity is alarming.
Supply chain attacks are evolving to specifically target AI coding assistants, using techniques like terminal escape codes that exploit the difference between human and machine parsing of output.
A consistent defensive pattern emerges across multiple disclosures: treat all external/retrieved content as untrusted data and enforce tool-call policies outside the model's decision loop.
Legal and regulatory pressure on AI companies is intensifying, with state-level lawsuits and federal executive actions both addressing AI risk disclosure and governance.
The OWASP agentic AI governance update signals maturing industry frameworks for translating AI safety principles into auditable controls.
